For the purpose of computing KTM, an intelligent searching-intelligent backtracking algorithm, which overcomes the shortages of the traditional searching-backtracking algorithm and improves the efficiency of computing KTM, is proposed. The details of the image are blurred and the information of texts is hidden in the image by using our algorithm. The experiments show that the image is approximately invariable in collectivity and it seems to be degraded by some noise. Therefore, the scrambled image does not easily stimulate other people's desire to decrypt it. By means of this, the security of the image and the information hidden into it are increased. This is propitious to transmitting security of image details and confidential texts.

articleTitle: Design of resilient guaranteed cost controllers for a class of generalized systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper deals with the design of resilient output guaranteed cost controllers for a class of generalized systems. The sufficient condition for guaranteed cost control is derived when there exists perturbation in controller gain. Based on LMI, we give an approach to design dynamic output feedback controller. Numerical example shows that the result given in this paper is very effective.

articleTitle: Compact genetic algorithm mutated by bit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Based on Harik's (1999) compact genetic algorithm, a kind of improved compact genetic algorithm mutated by bit is presented, which greatly improved the search ability. This paper also studies the performance of the improved algorithm. The experimental results show the superiority and efficiency of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive reference model tracking control of electrode systems of arc furnace
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Proposes an adaptive reference model tracking control system design approach for the electrode regulator system of an arc furnace. First the general description of this system is presented, in which the nonlinear part of the reference model is replaced by the identification result of the controlled system, then the existing conditions of the tracking control scheme is discussed. Based on that, the design of a feedforward control matrix and the iterative regulative algorithm of the feedback control matrix are put forward, which may lead the system to meet a good tracking performance. The simulation result has verified the effectiveness of the proposed scheme for a nonlinear system.

articleTitle: An ultrasonic obstacle avoidance system for fire fighting robot
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: For the purpose of protecting fire fighters from extreme danger in petrochemical, chemical dangerous product, toxicoid or exploder fire accidents, an unmanned firefighting robot, the first one in China, is developed in Mingguang fire fighting equipment factory of Anhui province, In this paper, an ultrasonic obstacle avoidance system used for fire fighting robot is presented. To meet the need of obstacle detection in hostile fire field under heavy smoke and high temperature condition, the transducer, STC circuit and anti-jamming processing are specially designed. Experiment on fire fighting robot prove the efficiency of the system. It also can be used to similar mobile robot systems.

articleTitle: A study on singularity avoidance and robust control of redundant robot
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Up to the present, a number of performance indices have been proposed for measure of dexterity of manipulators. There are many problems connected to the physical and mathematical meanings of these measures. In this paper, a new performance index considering aspect maintenance, computational burden, representation of an identical unit without regard to the robot and the effectiveness of the algorithm is proposed. This performance index is called the reduced minor index. Inverse kinematics is indispensable to robot control. The singularity-robust inverse is used and it offers a feasible motion close to the desired trajectory even at or in the neighborhood of singular points. Control of the redundant robot utilizing the upper reduced minor index and singularity-robust inverse is applied to the a 4 DOF wire-driven robot. The effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm is illustrated with simulation and experiment results.

articleTitle: PCSCW: P2P-based computer supported cooperative work research
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Until recently, most computer and network supported cooperative work systems are based on Web technologies, which is a client-server or centralized network model. The emergence and increasing adoption of peer-to-peer (P2P) offer a potential for the researchers of collaborative technologies, both as an enabling infrastructure and a platform for integration with existing end-user environments. This paper describes a peer-to-peer-based computer supported cooperative work (PCSCW) system that attempts to exploit the potential by extending the P2P to provide a set of basic facilities for collaborative information sharing.

articleTitle: Ant colony optimization for intelligent scheduling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A novel ant colony optimization algorithm was proposed for the scheduling problem in multiproduct chemical batch process, including a critical block based neighborhood structure in local search procedure to reduce the searching space of the problem, an ants-seed strategy, a stagnation step out mechanism and a pheromone trail limit mechanism in pheromone updating procedure to avoid stagnation. In the proposed algorithm, the pheromone acts as an indirect communication media among the ant colony. Guided by the pheromone, all the ants converge to good tours in the sense of probability. Comparisons with other well-performed algorithms on Taillard's benchmark problems (1993) show that our algorithm is more efficient and has stronger adaptability and robustness.

articleTitle: Rough set based decision tree
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Decision tree is widely used in machine learning. One important step in construction of a decision tree is how to select appropriate attributes as nodes of the tree. There are many approaches to selection of attributes. In this paper, we present a new approach to selection of attributes for construction of decision tree based on the rough set theory. Decision trees constructed by the presented approach tend to have simpler structure and higher classification accuracy from a statistical point of view than the entropy-based method under some conditions. Some data sets from UCI machine learning database repository are then used to test the two methods, which from application perspective instantiates the performance of rough set-based method. In the paper we also give an algorithm in a recursive form for the construction of decision tree.

articleTitle: Hybrid algorithm for job-shop scheduling problem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A hybrid algorithm of a genetic algorithm and tabu search is proposed to solve the job-shop scheduling problem in this paper. Tabu search acts as the mutation of the genetic algorithm, and implements the optimal process on individuals independently before the crossover operator operates them. A performance comparison of the proposed method with the better genetic algorithm and other heuristics is adopted to prove its efficiency based on the famous job-shop benchmark problem. The numerical experiments have shown its better optimal performance.

articleTitle: The energy saving control of air condition system in intelligent building
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: An energy saving control system of variable-air-volume air conditioner in intelligence building is formulated in this paper. It reaches good control effect and energy efficiency by making the best of the advantages of intelligence building. During the cooling preparation period, a neural network is used. In the regulating period, the air volume is decided by means of feed forward control. The previous turning off period is determined in the way of penalty function.

articleTitle: Robust H/sub /spl infin// control of interval systems using the delta operator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of robust stabilization of interval systems using the delta operator. Base on a kind of equivalent presentation of the interval systems, some sufficient conditions of robust stabilization of the systems are derived. The state feedback control for robust stabilization can be obtained by solving Riccati inequalities, which can stabilize the systems and guarantee a prescribed H/sub /spl infin// performance on attenuation of all admissible parameter uncertainties. The proposed approach can unify the related results of the continuous and discrete interval systems into the delta framework.

articleTitle: Identification-compensation approach for unknown disturbances via the estimate model of numerical differentiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Researching the characteristic of macroscopical motion, numerical differentiation is introduced to describe the dynamics of an unknown kinematic process, then the estimation model of numerical differentiation (NDEM) is constructed. Robust and simple models can be created by this approach for various applications, and it is easy to select suitable estimation algorithms to satisfy estimate quality. In the paper, NDEM is established for the guidance process of spacecraft rendezvous and docking (RVD) disturbed by unknown inputs, the kinematic parameters of RVD are captured for guiding outputs, and the unknown disturbances are estimated for active compensation. Simulation results show that NDEM is a robust model for obtaining accurate state estimation, and the precision of RVD guidance is immune from the unknown disturbances by the compensated control law.

articleTitle: An open industrial robot based on SERCOS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The paper presents a type of open industrial robot which is designed for processing armor plates of ship. It is the first robot based on SERCOS in China. With a so-called water-fire procedure, the robot can make an original plate the desirable shape. To deal with the diversity of the plates and the unexpected distortion during the processing, we promote a method called "measure instruct processing". The implementation of self-adaptive processing is discussed in the article.

articleTitle: Adaptive iterative feedback control for nonlinear system with unknown high-frequency gain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: An adaptive iterative feedback control approach is proposed for a class of single-input, single-output uncertain nonlinear systems with completely unknown high-frequency feedback gain. Unlike the common iterative learning control that requires some preconditions of stability on the learning gain, the adaptive iterative feedback control obtains the convergence through the change of high-frequency feedback gain in a Nussbaum-type function. This paper shows the repetitive tracking error sequence is asymptotic to zero when the iterative sequence i /spl rarr/ /spl infin/. Simulation is presented to show the validity of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: A robot simulation, monitoring and control system based on network and Java3D
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper introduces a robot simulation, monitoring and control system based on network and Java3D. When this system is connected with off-line programming module, users can program a robot by the legible robot language off-line, and finally download the robot instructions to the controller. When the system is connected with the robot controller via network, the status of the robot can be displayed in 3D-simulation mode, and the behavior of the robot can be monitored dynamically, and the authorized user can also control the action of the robot through the network as well. This paper describes the technique and method implementing executable interactive robot 3D simulation based on the Java platform, using Java3D for 3D visualization in combination with VRML for external robot representation in detail. This system can run on any operating system that supports JVM, and realizes the concept of "Write Once, Run Anywhere". This paper also discusses robot instruction, instruction interpreter and offline programming, and introduces the functional actualization of the 3D graphic simulation, monitoring and control system. Fully implemented cases include using this system under Linux and Windows operation system, and applying to PT500 and PT600 robot.

articleTitle: Adaptive method for low velocity moving target detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In radar signal processing, when a target moves with a low velocity, it generates so small a Doppler frequency shift that the target reflected signals are submerged by clutter signals, and the radar cannot detect the target, especially under low signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) environments. Because of its good performance in intelligent signal processing, an adaptive method is used to eliminate the clutter signals from the received signals in the signal's power spectrum figure according to the power spectrum distribution of the clutter.

articleTitle: Evolutionary algorithm for parameter identification inverse problems in parabolic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: We study a general evolutionary methodology for parameter identification problems in parabolic systems. Using EAs (evolutionary algorithms) avoids some of the weaknesses of traditional gradient-based analytical search methods including the difficulty in constructing well-defined mathematical models directly from the practical inverse problem, and easily getting trapped or oscillating between local minima and thus failing to produce useful solutions. An evolutionary algorithm for constructing a spatially varying diffusion parameter from observed data is proposed. By spline theory, we approximate the infinite dimensional inverse problem by a problem in the finite dimensional space. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Automatic separation of overlapping objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm based on mathematical morphology to separate overlapping objects automatically, which locates their linking points by the distance transform and dilation. It develops the design and implementation of the approach. In particular, it applies the technique to the problem of separating liver cells in hepatitis pathology images. The experiments show that the technique is fast and the separated results are satisfactory.

articleTitle: Advance in discrete-time sliding mode variable structure control theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Recent studies and developments of discrete-time variable structure control (DVSC) theory are summarized in this paper. Some control strategies of DVSC are analyzed. Two problems in DVSC-time-delay and chattering are discussed in detail. Finally, the prospective trends of DVSC are suggested.

articleTitle: Stability analysis and design of fuzzy control systems based on interval approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Based on the equivalent representation of interval matrix, the stability problem of fuzzy control system is converted into the robust stability problem of linear system with time-varying uncertainty. A necessary and sufficient condition for the quadratic stability of T-S fuzzy system is given, then, the controller design procedure is shown. In the case that the input matrices are identical, a necessary and sufficient condition for the quadratic stabilizability of the system is obtained, the fuzzy controller can be constructed directly. Simulation result shows the effectiveness and advantage of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An intelligent information retrieval system model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: On the basis of analyzing the problems of a traditional search engine, the article suggests a model based on a three layers C/S framework for a personal intelligent information retrieval system. In addition the article presents the framework and characteristic of this system model and discusses the partitioning of the system function module. According to the model, the off-line browsing and full-text in the local database as well as the intelligent search and personal information retrieval on the Internet should be able to realized.

articleTitle: A new regularization learning method for improving generalization capability of neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: When the network structure has been determined, it is very effective when regulation methods are used to improve generalization capability. However, there are some obvious drawbacks: long computation time, and difficulty in parameter control. The paper proposes a novel method that dynamically tunes the regularization coefficient by fuzzy rule inference, effectively determining the fuzzy inference rules and membership functions. Furthermore, it compares the method with the traditional BP algorithm and the fixed regularization coefficients method. The proposed method has the merits of the highest precision, rapid convergence, and the best generalization capability. Finally, it indicates that the proposed method is a very effective method by several nonlinear function approximation and pattern classification examples.

articleTitle: The pattern recognition of non-destructive testing based on HMM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A method of fault pattern recognition based on signal processing and pattern recognition. A hidden signal processing and characteristic reconstructed is presented Markov model which is scatter output and one rank is in this paper. Hidden Markov model (HMM),which is initially employed in the field of speech signal processing is introduced into fault pattern recognition of nondestructive testing(NDT), which lets a fault in aviation material be reconstructed automatically with the help of computer analysis and control system. It brings practical application for aviation material quality and safety use.

articleTitle: Application of fuzzy control theory to direct-heating furnace control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: On the basis of bias-flow analysis and the tackling method, a control scheme is present to resolve the bias-flow problem. Three fuzzy controllers are built, based on the three pipes' absolute temperature-difference as the input, the openness of the valve as the controlled object. After realizing this control scheme, the problem of bias-flow is resolved satisfactorily. The coked pipes are burned once a year, and almost no-coking occurs. We have been using this control scheme up to now for seven years and there is no need to replace the heating-pipes at all. The new design method of discrete fuzzy controller presented in this paper can also resolve the bias-flow problem in other fluid distribution control systems.

articleTitle: The research of fault diagnosis for fuel injection system of diesel engine with ANN based on rough sets theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The core content of rough set theory is introduced, and the discrete method of continuous attribute value based on the Kohonen neural network is given. The rough set theory is used to simplify the attribute parameter reflecting operating conditions of a diesel engine, and a RBF neural network is used to realize automatic fault classification and fault diagnosis for the fuel injection system of a diesel engine. The example is shown that the system's ANN input node number can be reduced.

articleTitle: Controlling bifurcation and chaos in Internet congestion control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The TCP congestion control plus random early detection (RED) queue management can be modeled as a discrete-time dynamical system which can create complex bifurcating and chaotic behavior. Based on the basic features of the TCP-RED model, we propose a robust adaptive RED algorithm for controlling bifurcation and chaos in Internet congestion control system.

articleTitle: Optimization method of modification coefficients of cylindrical gear pair having hard tooth flanks in closed drive based on genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The reasonable and optimal selection of modification coefficients of cylindrical gear pair having hard tooth flanks in a closed drive is beneficial to improving their properties, for example, the load capacity and scuffing load capacity, and so on. The optimization method of modification coefficients of cylindrical gear pair having hard tooth flanks in a closed drive based on the genetic algorithm is put forward. The method described is proved feasible by a given optimal design example.

articleTitle: The design on credit decision mechanism (CDM) from opportunity benefit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, we establish a nonlinear programming model on credit decision. We introduce the theory and methods of incentive mechanism design in the study of an entrepreneur who pursues opportunity benefits with imperfect information. We derive a concrete optimal credit decision mechanism (CDM) under a mortgage loan. We also discuss the problem of credit rationing and the CDM involving rationing and non-rationing, respectively. In addition, we suggest that the bank cannot make the decision in providing the loan or denying the applicant.

articleTitle: Design of linear-phase digital filters on frequency unequal sample
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, a method and principle for designing linear-phase digital IIR filter based on linear-phase FIR filter is presented. First, a linear-phase digital FIR filter is designed by using unequal sampling theory in the frequency domain. Then in order to satisfy the specialty of the given filter, the amount and frequency positions of these sampling can be simply, directly and easily adjusted while the amount of sampling in time domain does not change. And then a linear-phase digital IIR filter that has the same amplitude with the above-mentioned FIR filter can be obtained by using model reduction based on the impulse-response GRAM matrix.

articleTitle: A novel sliding mode servo controller for hard disk drives
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper presents a novel sliding mode seek controller for hard disk servos. A 3/sup rd/-order velocity reference profile is introduced to improve the 2/sup nd/ ones in the conventional Proximate Time-Optimal Servomechanism (PTOS). The proposed approach eliminates the mode-switching mechanism and realizes the smooth mode transit from seeking to following without overshoot. Moreover, the servo system is chattering free. It is well known that PTOS is not effective in short stroke seeks. The proposed control scheme significantly improves the short stroke seeks. In particular, the seek time is dramatically reduced by 2%-60%. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is verified in experiments.

articleTitle: Global stabilization controller design for discrete-time bilinear systems with time-delays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper discusses global asymptotic stabilization for a class of MIMO discrete-time bilinear systems with multiple time-delays. Based on LaSalle invariant principle and the separation principle, sufficient conditions (with delay-dependent) for global asymptotic stabilization are presented. Both saturated state feedback and saturated full-order dynamic output feedback controllers are constructed, respectively.

articleTitle: Stable fuzzy adaptive control for a class of nonlinear system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A new hybrid fuzzy adaptive control scheme is presented systematically for a class of affine nonlinear unknown systems using Lyapunov stability theory. Because of combining fuzzy control with fuzzy identification, it demands little pre-knowledge about the plant models, so the method is generally applicable. In order to overcome the problem of the model mismatch, a compensation control term is introduced into the controller. Based on the conception, approximate error coefficient, the degree of accuracy of the fuzzy identifier can be described quantitatively. According to this, the identifier can be designed easily and suitably.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of a learning feedforward controller using Bartlet window
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A learning feedforward controller (LFFC) using the Bartlet window function is proposed for a better tracking control of linear system over a finite time interval. LFFC is applied as a feedforward controller to the existing feedback controller. This paper demonstrates that using a simple window function-Bartlet (Fejer or triangular) window in signal processing, the design of a learning feedforward controller reduces to determining only two design parameters: the learning gain and the number of point in the window. Convergence analysis is presented together with a design procedure.

articleTitle: Parameter identification method for stochastic continuous system via wavelets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper studies the parameter identification problem of linear and bilinear continuous time stochastic systems based on wavelet approximation theory. The computation formulas of the correlative matrix of wavelet approximation coefficients of the Wiener process are given. Based on these results, the Markov estimation of parameters and its recursion algorithm are presented.

articleTitle: The principle and application of synergetic pattern recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The paper first expounds the principle of synergetic pattern recognition. Then it discusses the implementation techniques of the pathology image classification system based on the principle in detail. What's more, to resolve the problem that the synergetic neural network is weak in recognizing new test samples, it presents the information superposition self-learning algorithm based on a genetic algorithm. The experimental results prove the effectivity of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Mixed l/sub 1//H/sub 2/ control for MIMO systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper we consider the mixed l/sub 1//H/sub 2/ control problem for multiple input-multiple output (MIMO) discrete-time systems. This problem is formulated as minimizing the l/sub 1/-norm of a closed-loop transfer matrix while maintaining the H/sub 2/-norm of another closed-loop transfer matrix at prescribed level. The continuity property of the optimal value respect to changes in the H/sub 2/-norm constraint is studied. The existence of the optimal solutions of mixed l/sub 1//H/sub 2/ problem is proved. Since the solution of the mixed l/sub 1//H/sub 2/ problem is based on the scaled-Q method, it avoids the zero interpolation difficulties. The convergent upper and lower bounds can be obtained by solving a sequence of finite dimensional nonlinear programming for which many efficient numerical optimization techniques exist. A simulation example shows the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Research on the key technology of integrating e-commerce with CIMS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The problem solving of the heterogeneous environment during integration of e-commerce with CIMS is discussed in detail. The environment uses the Web database and Java to realize automatic information exchange in B to B commerce. It uses CORBA to solve the encapsulation problem of legacy systems and dynamic e-mail to realize automatic information exchange in B to C commerce.

articleTitle: An improved time delay DMC and its application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: An improved time delay dynamic matrix control (DMC) predictive model is established according to the actual process of a paper-making machine, whose dynamic performance is analysed and studied. The simulation study shows that the improved dynamic matrix control is applicable on the dynamic performance of paper-making machine and shortening the response time, with excellent anti-interference capability and good robustness.

articleTitle: Relay-based friction identification in frequency domain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper addresses the application of a dual relay feedback approach towards the identification of frictional effects in servo-mechanisms. The friction model consists of Coulomb (including possibly directional Coulomb or load bias) and viscous friction components, both of which can be automatically extracted from suitably designed relay experiments. At the same time, the dynamical model of the servo-mechanical system can be obtained from the experiments. These models will be directly useful in the design of the feedback controller and the friction compensator. Results from a simulation study are presented to illustrate the practical appeal of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Study on manufacturing resource integrated system of the distributed manufacturing dynamic dispatching
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The essence of dynamic dispatching of distributed manufacturing is analyzed in the paper. Then, the conditions of a manufacturing resource integrated system of the distributed manufacturing dynamic dispatching are put forward. After a model of the manufacturing resource integrated system is set up according to the theory of multi-agents, the topological graph method is used to explain the information flow. Finally, the theoretical basis of the construction of the manufacturing resource integrated system of the distributed manufacturing dynamic dispatching is discussed in detail.

articleTitle: "Soft assignment algorithm" in maneuvering targets tracking
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The optimal solution of the "assignment problem" in maneuvering target tracking (MTT) is how to associate measurements with tracks correctly. It is critical in MTT. The earlier "traditional assignment algorithm" has poor performance because it does not consider missing and new targets. The modern augment assignment algorithm overcomes the two shortcomings above, but at the same time, the risk of error association probability becomes higher. This paper presents a new assignment algorithm-"soft assignment". It need not consider missing and new targets while it is an optimal solution based on the following two criteria: (1) the correct association probability is high; (2) the number of associations is near to the actual ones. The two criteria are presented in the form of function and the optimal solution using "soft assignment" can also be obtained.

articleTitle: The predictive model of bubble point based on neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The calculation of bubble point plays an important role in the chemical process of separation. Traditional methods are quite complicated, and they are also time-consuming tasks. In the paper, the bubble points in trays of a methanol distillation column are first calculated by process simulation software named Design II. Then, some of the data are used to train a backpropagation (BP) neural network and a radial basis function (RBF) neural network respectively. Finally neural networks are used to predict the left bubble points. The result indicates that the predicted data are in good agreement with the experimental data obtained by Design II, and the speed of the RBF neural network is better than that of the BP neural network.

articleTitle: Adaptive neural control for a class of nonlinearly parametric time-delay systems: first order case
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive neural controller for a class of first-order time-delay nonlinear systems with unknown nonlinearities is proposed. Based on WNN (wavelet neural network) online approximation model, a state-feedback adaptive controller is obtained by constructing an novel Integral-type Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional. The key assumption is that the time-delay term of the systems satisfies a certain inequality condition. The proposed method guarantees semi-global uniform ultimate boundedness for the adaptive closed-loop systems. An example is provided to illustrate the application of the approach.

articleTitle: [%P] prediction and control model for oxygen-converter process at the end point based on adaptive neuro-fuzzy system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: According to the process and data from spot, the methodology for [%P] prediction and control is discussed. A self-organizing network has been utilized to classify 303 heats from spot, which makes the analysis of the influence of steelmaking variables on [%P] possible. The control variables for the [%P] prediction and control model were determined with the analysis. A model of [%P] prediction and control has been established for BOF at the end point based on an adaptive neuro-fuzzy system. The results show that this model has good performance on prediction and control for [%P] in the BOF process. The R-value of model output and actual [%P] in the experiment reaches 0.5867. The hit rate of the model in the precision /spl plusmn/0.003% [%P] is 79.21%. With this model, if the [%P] was controlled by the model with the value less than target by 0.004%, 91% of heats are up to grade in regard to [%P].

articleTitle: An affine nonlinear control approach to mobile robot with nonholonomic orthogonal-wheels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, we present an affine nonlinear control approach based on the differential geometric point of view, according to the tracking problem of the mobile robot with nonholonomic orthogonal-wheels. This approach can not only be applied to nonlinear control system, but also to a nonlinear control system with strong coupling. The simulation results show that the approach has a very effective result on the tracking problem of the mobile robot.

articleTitle: An improved neural networks with transient chaos method for job-shop scheduling problems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Having considered all the constraints of the job-shop scheduling problem (JSP), we present a new computational energy function of Hopfield neural networks for JSP. By introducing transient chaos and time-variant gain, an improved method to solve JSP by a neural network model with transient chaos is proposed, which can avoid Hopfield neural networks being sucked into local minima. The simulation results show that the modified method not only has the ability of searching for the global minimum, but can also converge to minimum quickly. More importantly, it can keep the steady output of neural networks as a feasible solution for JSP.

articleTitle: Application of genetic algorithm to optimize product structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: After careful analysis of production, technology and management of a coal preparation plant, the mathematical model of product structure optimization for the coal preparation plant is constructed. Then the principle and steps of solving the product structure using a genetic algorithm are given. Finally, an example is given to verify the practicability of this method and which shows that this method can supply scientific laws for an enterprise to implement production planning.

articleTitle: A QoS-aware networked telerobotic system architecture: AeQTA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper analyzes the characteristics of the networked telerobotic system in comparison with the video conferencing system which is a typical case of distribute multimedia systems. Then, by taking some end-to-end quality of service (QoS) control models and their characteristics for reference, it proposes an adaptive end-to-end QoS architecture for the networked teleoperation AeQTA.

articleTitle: Internet-enhanced automation in micro environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Developments in the Internet have significantly increased the human capability to reach and obtain information from remote locations. In parallel, the advent of micro sensors and actuators makes it possible for humans to sense and act in a micro-environment. Combined, the Internet and MEMS will produce a new technology for humans to sense and act in remote micro-environments, allowing the potential development of micro teleoperation and micro automation technologies. We present our ongoing development of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) sensors that can be used for force-reflective control of micromechanical devices over the Internet. Internet based teleoperation between Hong Kong and Michigan State was demonstrated using an event-based control scheme, which ensured stability and synchronization. Control was enhanced by multimedia feedback, which included, in addition to the traditional video, force feedback.

articleTitle: ECG partition based on the wavelet pyramid algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Through a multi-resolution analysis of the Holter electrocardiogram (ECG) phase, the ECG partition is implemented by using the pyramid. algorithm. The calculation results demonstrate that the segmentation has good accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimal control method of stretching process of solar wings on multibody spacecraft
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The optimal attitude control problem of spacecraft during the stretching process of solar wings is discussed in this paper. A mathematical model of the system is established by using the multibody dynamics and optical control theory. An algorithm of control for the stretching process is proposed, considering the nonholonomic behavior of the system. The effectiveness of the approach is shown by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of Yi Chang production-sales computer system based on CIMS structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The computer system for the production and sales of Shanghai Bao Steel Yi Chang Steel Strip Co., Ltd. is designed and developed. The CIMS structure is considered and some functions of which are incorporated in order to shorten the developing time. This system was implemented and applied successfully in the factory.

articleTitle: Fuzzy normal proposition logic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A new logical structure, fuzzy normal proposition logic, is defined in this paper. When used to describe objectives things, it is quite near to their original appearances, and may well be realized in popular computers. Still, we discussed some properties of the logical structure, and establish a fuzzy normal proposition probability space.

articleTitle: Two-step procedure for subspace-based process modeling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A two-step procedure for subspace-based process modeling is proposed. Firstly, a deterministic model is built as a basic control-oriented process model, which uses plant test data. Then the historical operational data are used to build the stochastic model for closed-loop control by subspace identification. Finally, the stochastic model serves as a modified form of the basic model for adaptive controller design.

articleTitle: The modeling and simulation of ship main engine based on neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper presents a ship main engine model with RBF neural network using the actual data of MAN B&W 6L80MC ship engine. The master-slave simulator for ship engine and control system is developed based on the engine model, the upper computer is a PC with human-machine interface, and the lower computer is a microcontroller to control the engine model through simulation console. The simulators have been opened for training students and seamen at several maritime colleges and ship enterprises in China since 2000.

articleTitle: Recognition and classification of metallography via fractional dimension
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper gives some basic algorithms to obtain fractional dimension of fractal through changing the observation scale. Some fractional dimensions of metallographies are calculated. The main aim is to recognize and classify the metallographies via fractional dimension and provide the conditions to control the quality of steel.

articleTitle: Output feedback fuzzy adaptive control for a class of large-scale nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Hybrid stable output feedback decentralized control schemes are presented for a class of uncertain large scale nonlinear systems for which the state variables are unavailable for feedback. These hybrid indirect control algorithms consist of three different control components. The adaptive fuzzy logic system plays a dominant role to maintain the whole closed-loop stability. Being the auxiliary compensation, a sliding mode control is designed to compensate for the interactions between subsystems and a H/sup /spl infin// control is designed to attenuate fuzzy approximation errors. Thus, this hybrid output feedback adaptive fuzzy decentralized controller can guarantee the global stability of the closed-loop, and achieve a good tracking performance as well. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: A flowshop scheduling algorithm to minimize total weighted completion time
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The paper considers the problem of minimizing total weighted completion time in a flowshop. A heuristic algorithm with worst-case bound m is given. For m = 2, if jobs have agreeable weights i.e. where p/sub i/ /spl les/ p/sub j/ implies w/sub i/ /spl ges/ w/sub j/, (i, j = 1, 2, /spl middot//spl middot//spl middot/, n). The worst-case bound is 2/spl beta///spl alpha/+/spl beta/, where /spl alpha/ and /spl beta/ denote the minimum and maximum processing time of all operations. For some special cases, the polynomial algorithms are given.

articleTitle: Blind separation of sources based on genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Based on a genetic algorithm and variance normalization of output signals, this paper proposes two new methods for blind separation of sources. Simulation results illustrate that the method using a hybrid genetic algorithm not only keeps unsupervised, adaptive learning and the robust advantages of the known improved Herault-Jutten (H-J) (Jutten and Herault, 1991) algorithm, but also guarantees global convergence and less training time.

articleTitle: Robust H/sub /spl infin// control for uncertain stochastic time-delayed systems with nonlinear actuators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The robust H/sub /spl infin// control problem for uncertain stochastic time-delayed systems with nonlinear actuators is considered. The uncertainties in the systems are assumed to satisfy a specific matching condition. The time delays exist in the state as well as control input. A new stochastic robust stabilizable criterion and a sufficient condition for the existence of the stochastic robust stabilizing control law are derived. The delay-independent memoryless robust H/sub /spl infin// controllers are constructed to stabilize the given system in terms of a group of linear matrix inequalities. The complex degree of numerical computing for HJI inequality can be overcome by using the LMI tool.

articleTitle: On stability analysis of the multirate multivariable predictive control systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, a predictive control algorithm is developed for multirate multivariable system in which the sampling periods of outputs and holding periods of inputs are all different. In order to make full use of the information and reduce the burden of the computer, the optimization is done as long as there is at least a new measured output since the time k and one input that need to be updated. By grouping the variables in a frame period into vectors, the characteristic equation is derived. Thus, the stability condition of the closed loop system is obtained for the system presented in this paper. Simulation results indicate that the method is effective.

articleTitle: Confirming the location and moving trend of small motion robot by color picture division
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, confirmation of the location and moving trend of small moving robot has been studied by color picture division under the condition of obtaining picture information by full vision. The method of chroma transform and dia-dimension array of Y, U, V have been adopted when the color picture signal was obtained, whose result was compared with that by color picture signal realized by the threshold value of Y, U, V. and the test error of barycenter coordinate of robot has been analyzed when testing the location and moving trend of the moving robot.

articleTitle: Intelligence aided advanced process control of industrial distillation column
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper represents a successful application of Advanced Process Control (APC) with predictive functional control and fuzzy compensation of the temperature difference of rectifying sections in an aromatics distillation column. The application of APC improves disturbance rejection and operation of the columns and increases the recovery of aromatics while reducing energy consumption.

articleTitle: H/sub /spl infin// identification for nonlinear system based on generalized frequency response function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Based on the GFRF (generalized frequency response function), H/sub /spl infin// identification for nonlinear system is investigated using the set membership identification theory. We applied the three-order truncated Volterra series to describe the nonlinear system, and accomplished the model identification by the Householder transformation that is a kind of orthogonal decomposition, and then derived the GFRF of the system. Moreover, by means of the set membership identification we give a measure of the model perturbation in a form well suited for H/sub /spl infin//-control methodologies. The effectiveness of the proposed procedure is tested on the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: An LMI approach to design robust fault detection observers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this contribution, the robust fault detection observer design problem for LTI systems with both disturbances and modelling errors are studied. The basic idea of our study is to split the system state into plant state and the so called fault state, while the fault state is used to diagnose the occurrence of the fault. Then the main task of FDI becomes the fault state optimal estimation problem. Based on this, the FDI observer design problem is finally formulated as a two-objective H/sub /spl infin//-optimization and the LMI approach is developed. An illustrated numerical example is also presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Study on prediction modeling of the artificial neural network from the combination of multivariate analysis and mean generation function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A mixed prediction model involving a significant period of a predictand the physical factors influencing the change of predictand is built based on an artificial neural network from the combination of multivariate analysis and mean generation function. The new model is found to have a higher predicative accuracy (due mainly to the reasonable analysis for prediction method), when compared to results from multivariate statistical model or mean generating function prediction model.

articleTitle: PD type of time delay filter design in the feedback control system to reduce high frequency noise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A new PD type time delay filter, which utilizes the time-delay filter effect, is introduced into the feedback control. It is shown that conventional P-controller equipped with an appropriate time-delay performs an average derivative action and thus can be insensitive to high-frequency noise. It also responds quickly to input changes. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this PD type of time delay filter.

articleTitle: Fuzzy controller and observer design for nonlinear system-LMI method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A fuzzy controller and observer design for a nonlinear system are studied based on LMI. The global asymptotically stable fuzzy controller and observer is gained, using the T-S fuzzy dynamic model approaching a nonlinear system and using a parallel distributed compensation method. The parameters of the fuzzy controller and fuzzy observer are obtained by the convex optimal method of LMI. The simulation of an inverted pendulum tested the efficiency of the design method.

articleTitle: Identification for integrating processes in the frequency domain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, a new identification method in the frequency domain from a relay-based test is proposed for integrating processes. In the relay test, only the very first period of oscillating input is implemented, which automatically results in a two-side pulse signal. The two-side pulse waveform contains enough larger spectrum magnitude over the important frequency range so that the process frequency responses can be accurately estimated at multiple points using the Fourier analysis method. Simulation examples are given to show both the effectiveness and practicality of the identification method for various integrating processes.

articleTitle: Autonomous robot soccer system based on hybrid architecture
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A reactive autonomous robot soccer system based on a hybrid architecture is proposed. According to the persisting time of the hidden state of the ball's visual information, the planning level reactively selects suitable tasks and behaviors. To deal with the hidden states of the visual information, the behavior level takes reactive behaviors with particular designs. The spontaneous switching among behaviors, planning the sequences of the behaviors implicitly, simplifies the planning of the behaviors and makes the system robust. Experiments and games indicate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A Web-based remote financial MIS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The article introduces the structure of a remote financial MIS, describes its main functions and modules, and provides the methods to build the system.

articleTitle: The analysis of the local search efficiency of genetic neural networks and the improvement of algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Several concepts, such as "locus fitness" and "locus influencing factors", and a coding norm of "maximizing the locus influencing factors" are proposed, based on which the local search efficiency of genetic neural networks is analyzed. To counter the problem that "locus influencing factors" are too small, we modify the algorithm by rising the probabilities of mutation and crossover to improve the optimum seeking performance.

articleTitle: Haptic display of contact states
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: During manual assembly or manipulation of objects, different contact states between the object held by the human operator and other objects in the environment should result in different kinds of haptic sensations to the operator. In this paper, we address haptic rendering by taking into account the type of contact state and the effects of friction and gravity. We present a method to model the haptic force and moment caused by a principal contact between a virtually "held" polyhedral solid and another virtual polyhedral solid. We further describe how to identify a contact state between the virtual objects in real time, which is essential for the corresponding haptic rendering. The feasibility of our methods are verified by experiments.

articleTitle: An open intelligent network based on Ethernet framework and its application to project
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: With the recent development of network technology, a whole open intelligent network scheme based on the Ethernet framework is presented. There are some discussions about how to establish an intelligent control network and how to carry out real-time monitoring and managing information. Also in this paper, the application to an intelligent mansion project is discussed.

articleTitle: Robust stabilization for a class of discrete-time systems with nonlinear perturbations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper discusses robust stabilization problem for a class of multi-input multi-output (MIMO) discrete-time linear systems with both state and control input contained nonlinear perturbations. The problem is solved via static output feedback. A unified approach is used to cast the problem into a convex optimization involving linear matrix inequality, the controller can robustly stabilize the systems and maximize the bound on the nonlinear perturbations.

articleTitle: A lie-resisting evaluation and decision method in virtual enterprise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In real applications of the virtual enterprise, there are many lies when agents negotiate with each other about tasks and rewards. To resist the lies, a general evaluation and decision model and a correspondent method are proposed. Negotiation data are not always trusted but evaluated by means of fuzzy reasoning to decide whether and how much we should rely on it. Because fuzzy rules are obtained based on data mining in former evaluation and decision data, the method is objective. Experiments demonstrate that the model is suitable and the method is effective and reliable.

articleTitle: Model predictive control for a class of hybrid system based on linear programming
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Aiming at the hybrid properties of an industrial process, predictive control based on a mixed logic dynamic model is presented to research a class of hybrid systems which comprises both logic and continuous controllers. The paper presents the algorithm for model predictive control based on 1-1 norm linear programming and the system's stability condition is also discussed. Simulation results show that the LP-based performance criterion has less computational time and cost than that of QP-based criteria. Thus the LP-based strategy is particularity well suited for solving control systems with large size and very stringent real-time requirement, which provides the complex industrial process with a new idea for the next generation.

articleTitle: Componentialization of learning system and its object-oriented programming implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper presents an idea for the research and developing of learning systems - componentialization. A learning system is to be componentialized into some blocks of special function, each cooperates with others by some standardized interfaces. The developing and research works of a learning system is to be assigned to specialists of different related domains. The object-oriented programming idea is naturally integrated. A learning system, a component of it, or even a problem, may be fit for the concept of an "object" in object-oriented programming and may be described by a C++ class. The programming language C++ helps make clear the idea of componentialization and describe the implementation of it. An example of an actual case of componentialized learning system is presented with successful application, to show its feasibility and efficiency.

articleTitle: Building agent-mediated teleservice system on J2EE platform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: E-commercialization and artificial intelligence approach are the development trends of manufacturing teleservice systems. In this paper, the authors show how to implement and integrate an agent-mediated teleservice application on the J2EE platform, and realize an e-commercialized teleservice. An ontology application for the teleservice system is also discussed.

articleTitle: Application of non-model controller in outlet temperature control of furnace
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The non-model controller shows different superiorities for the control of any production process without building mathematical model from other types of formula. In this paper, by using formulas from DCS and industrial control computers, we prove that the non-model controller is a high starting point, better adaptability and good robustness controller.

articleTitle: Robust fault-tolerant satisfied control for time-delay uncertain systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper deals with the methods of robust fault tolerant satisfied control for time-delay uncertain systems with actuator fault by using the approach of linear matrix inequality satisfying the condition of finite time bounded stability. The sufficient conditions which are able to realise robust fault tolerant satisfied control of the systems are obtained with both continuous time and discrete time cases, respectively. Furthermore, we obtain the results of robust fault-tolerant satisfied control with integrity for the actuator fault systems.

articleTitle: Design of a flexible robot assembly demo system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, a flexible robot assembly system designed for demonstrating advanced technologies, such as CAD/CAM, flexible assembly systems (FAS) and material management technology in CIMS is introduced. On the basis of a principle embodying flexibility of manufacturing and assembly, a system that can assemble two different kinds of products without any modification is designed. The system is composed of a CAD subsystem, mini 3D storage, a sculptor subsystem and one flexible robot assembly subsystem. Products to be assembled and assembly sequences are designed elaborately. The main equipment of the robot assembly subsystem such as the assembly robot, screw-on robot and conveyor are introduced and the design of an end hand and assembly worktable is discussed in detail. A distributed control mode is adopted in the system. Flow of software including material flow and information flow is described. Assembly experiments of automobile models show that the assembly line can complete assembling a product in three to five minutes.

articleTitle: The design and realization of fuzzy velocity controller for navigation and interactions in virtual environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: 3D interactions in virtual environment are an important research direction. Their realization depends mainly on the navigation in virtual environments. In this paper, the authors introduce the fuzzy algorithm and use it to design a navigation velocity controller, which can response to the user's mouse input. The test result indicates that it can identify the user's intension and improve the performance of navigation.

articleTitle: Identification and compensation of strategic missile guidance system error model based on the BP neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The error model of guidance system was established and inducted to nonlinear regression model in the paper. Based on the improved algorithm, the back-propagation neural network is applied to identify guidance system error model. The simulating data are used in the training of the neural network. The trained network should be used for the actual test data and error compensation. As a result, this method can improve the shooting accuracy of the missile.

articleTitle: A decoupling controller of genetic neural algorithm with improving function of adaptable degree
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: An improving function algorithm of the adaptable degree of a genetic algorithm is presented, on the basis of improving the adaptation degree function, a genetic neural controller is constituted. Moreover this method is validated using analysis, simulation and experiments of stoves.

articleTitle: Indirect adaptive neural networks control for a class of nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Based on sliding mode control theory and approximation capability of multilayer neural networks (MNNs), a design scheme of a indirect robust adaptive controller for a class of nonlinear systems is proposed in this paper. The scheme guarantees the global stability of the closed-loop system while the closed-loop system tracking error converges to zero.

articleTitle: A remote control system using Java and CORBA architecture
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Membranes hold promise as a new water treatment method of the future. In this study, a device is designed to test the efficiency of membranes. The device is implemented to be controlled remotely. An Internet based remote control system is implemented on the membrane test device to make the users access to it easier. When using the system, a remote operator only needs a general purpose computer with Internet connection to conduct a test. The engineering objective is to perform robust control over the Internet connection. A control architecture that combines computer and the membrane testing hardware is built. This system has two primary parts, the server part and the client part. A server is used to provide the application to the operator to control the hardware. The client part is executed on the remote operator's computer. The client uses a TCP/IP protocol to connect to the server through the Internet. Communication coordination between the client and the server is developed using Java and Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA).

articleTitle: Unconditional stability criteria for linear systems with multi-delays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, the stability of the linear system: x/spl dot//sub i/(t)=/spl Sigma//sub j=1//sup m/b/sub ij/x/sub j/(t)+c/sub ij/x/sub j/(t-/spl tau//sub ij/) b/sub ij//spl ges/0, c/sub ij//spl ges/0, i=1,2/spl middot//spl middot//spl middot/m is investigated by introducing the concept of /spl alpha/-bidiagonal dominance and, by using of the characteristics of the M-matrices, several new criteria are obtained.

articleTitle: An ANN model for SCR voltage regulator driven induction motor with dynamic loads
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A model for a SCR voltage regulator driven induction motor with dynamic loads is built, which is based on the Elman neural network with a regression unit, making use of dynamic backpropagation (BP) learning. The approach has advantages over the traditional BP method with resonance and slow convergence rate. Our simulations show that this method has a high convergence rate.

articleTitle: Train control information simulation for ATP of urban railway transit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Automatic train protection (ATP) system of urban railway transit is very important for safe operation, where the effective transmission of train control information is the most significant factor. In the research of nationalization for the ATP system, carried out by the Ministry of Constructions and Ministry of Railways of China, the frequency shift keying (FSK) approach is adopted to modulate the train control information, as it does not need to estimate the phase of the carrier wave. This paper introduces a computer simulation method of FSK, and solves some of the key techniques, such as how to make the FSK simulation into a real-time system with continuous phase as well as dynamically changed the codes and frequencies of FSK. The computer simulated FSK was implemented in an ATP simulation system and was shown to be effective.

articleTitle: Computer controlled synthesizing of superhard materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A hinge type six-anvil hydraulic press is the main equipment for the production of superhard materials. Relays are usually its electric controlling units with poor reliability and high rate of malfunction. The hydraulic press is controlled by a computer system in this paper, both pressure and temperature are dominated according to the relations with time. Its hardware is an STD industrial computer with SCM Intel8098; the software could be automatic or manual operating. The insolating transformer, power conditioner, and special supply for the STD bus are used to avoid interference of the energy supply system. In order to prevent the process pathway from interference, an optoelectronic coupler, twisted pair wires for long-distance current transmission are adopted. Furthermore, measures are adopted to avoid the interference of the electromagnetic field. Experiments demonstrate that the system has many merits such as high control precision, strong anti-interference ability, and high reliability.

articleTitle: Robust H/sub /spl infin// state feedback control with an /spl alpha/-stability constraint for uncertain time-delay systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of robust H/sub /spl infin// state feedback control with the /spl alpha/-stability constraint for linear time-delay systems with norm-bounded parameter uncertainties in all matrices of a state-space representation. The sufficient condition for the existence of the solutions to the problem is presented in terms of one linear matrix inequality (LMI). Through some manipulations and Schur complements, the controller design is reduced to a convex optimization problem. The solutions can be readily obtained using existing LMI Toolbox without pre-selecting any parameter. A numerical example is provided to illustrate the proposed design approach.

articleTitle: Classifier for chinese traditional medicine with high-dimensional and small sample-size data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The identification of Chinese traditional medicine is a difficult subject in pharmacology. The development of chemical measurement and pattern recognition make chemical pattern recognition possible. In the paper a new chemical pattern recognition method is proposed, in which a simple method called corresponding-peak distance calculation is used to compute the distance between samples for a nearest neighbor (NN) classifier, and a genetic algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of the NN classifier. With the proposed method, experiments are carried out on chromatogram data of Panax. The results indicate that the method can identify the medicine material of different harvest time or habitats, furthermore, this method which combines pattern matching, genetic algorithm and NN classifier is robust, accurate and easy to implement.

articleTitle: Expert-based multi-mode switching control for the temperature and humidity control system of archive establishment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: An expert-based multi-mode switching control for the temperature and humidity control system of archive establishment is proposed in this paper. This system possesses a two-level structure including: multi-mode switching controllers (MSC) in the lower level for basic control, and an expert supervisory system in the higher level for performance enhancement and energy saving. Due to its simple structure, the multi-mode switching controller is very easy to be designed or tuned. Moreover, it is very suitable for the temperature and humidity control system for its strong capacity to handle time-delays. The expert supervisory system implements an operation mode recognition and control approach selection to optimise the overall control and obtains an enhanced and robust performance in different operation modes. The performance analysis and simulation results show the practicability of the proposed system and its viability in the real archive establishment environment.

articleTitle: Quantitative feedback theory (QFT) based humanoid biped robot control design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper describes the design of joint motion control of humanoid biped robot, based on quantitative feedback theory and multi-objective optimization control. From the practical engineering viewpoint, an improved QFT method is presented and used in the controller design. An application example is described; simulation results of the joint motion control show stability, robustness, and the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Flying control system simulation modeling using Simulink
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A subsection modeling and dynamic switching method Is developed. First, the system is studied and the mathematical models for every time-period are set up. Then, the simulation models for every time-period are established. Finally, a m-function is designed which makes the simulation models for every time-period be linked and the system states be continuous. This method is applied to the simulation modeling of a flying control system, the simulation speed is greatly accelerated.

articleTitle: The implementation of active vibration control of flexible structure using DSP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper an active vibration control system of flexible beam system is presented by using the piezoelectric, which can be used as both sensors and actuators. The vibration restrain is realized by the TMS320F240 DSP based control system. Experimental results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of this kind of control strategy.

articleTitle: The development of an intelligent small paperless recorder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Inherited from the successful design of the large paperless recorder, the intelligent small paperless recorder has a modular structure. It also employs the same data acquisition module as the large paperless recorder does. It has a menu driven GUI (full Chinese language), eight multi-purpose input channels (all user configurable), 16-channel relay outputs and 2-channel analog outputs (V/mA). Though a MCS51 based MCU is used as the main controller, the limitations of 64K RAM and ROM of this kind of MCU have been conquered through page mapping and code banking technologies. The paper describes how to accomplish this breakthrough from the aspects of hardware and software design.

articleTitle: New condition for global exponential stability of neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, based on globally Lipschitz continuous activation functions, new conditions ensuring existence, uniqueness and global exponential stability of the equilibrium point of neural networks are obtained.

articleTitle: Evolutionary robot behavior via natural selection based on neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The traditional fitness function based methodology of artificial evolution is argued to be inadequate for the construction of entities with behaviors novel to their designers. Evolutionary emergence via natural selection (without an explicit fitness function) is the way forward. This paper primarily considers the question of what to evolve, and focuses on principles of developmental modularity in neural networks. To develop and test the ideas, an artificial world containing autonomous organisms has been created and is described. Experimental results show that the developmental system is well suited to long-term incremental evolution.
