Novel emergent strategies are identified both from an observer's perspective and in terms of their neural mechanisms.

articleTitle: Searching for symmetric permutations of binary patterns set with genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Symmetry is a powerful tool to reduce the freedom degrees of a problem. However, the applicability of the symmetry tool strongly depends on the possibility to calculate the symmetries of the system. General searching methods, e.g., ergodic searching, is unpractical for a high-dimensional system since the order of the symmetric group grows with n, where n is the dimension of the system. We propose an approach based on genetic algorithms to search for the symmetric permutations of a binary patterns set. Calculations for five kinds of dimensional pattern set are also given. Results show that the majority of symmetric permutations can be found within an acceptable time for a high-dimensional pattern set by the new approach, which makes it possible to study and design high-dimensional artificial neural networks by the method of symmetry.

articleTitle: A meter for on-line measurement of melting point of aluminum electrolyte
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper investigates on-line measurement of the melting point of aluminum electrolyte by use of a common K type thermocouple, which is based on the heat transfer during the phase transformation. The hardware and software of the intelligent meter for the measurement are also introduced. This meter consists of data collection, data conversion, data processing, data display and data communication. The single-chip 80C31 is the central processing unit and A/D574 performs the A/D conversion. The liquid crystal display and the key were connected by the chip 81C55.

articleTitle: Protocol analysis based on EPr/TN net
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Protocol analysis is the center of protocol engineering science, and the performance of computer networks can be evaluated through it. A protocol is analyzed for quality and quantity using EPr/TN for qualitative analysis. The EPr/TN model is given and some properties relative to the protocol can be deduced; quantitative analysis is made through the performance expression that can be obtained by the EPr/TN model describing the parameter relation of protocol flows.

articleTitle: The insufficiency and improving methods of GA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)

articleTitle: The design and implementation of an Internet information extracting system for enterprise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A prototype system based on agent mechanism is presented and implemented to improve the speed and accuracy in extracting Internet information. The prototype system employs agents as the basic components and organizes them in a federal framework. The task can be done with the autonomy and corporation of the agents. The technology employing in the system including secure channel-firewall and automatic transformation of Web site structure promote the security and easy of use of the system. The products and applications base on the prototype system are used in practice and the feasibility and validity of the system are confirmed.

articleTitle: Robust absolute stability for interval Lur'e control systems with several independent stationary components
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The problem of robust absolute stability for interval Lur'e type control systems with several independent nonlinear stationary elements is considered by Lyapunov function method. Some sufficient conditions of robust absolute stability for interval Lur'e direct control systems and interval Lur'e indirect control systems are respectively given. Previous results are extended and improved.

articleTitle: The research of networking enterprise modeling system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The evolution of network gives an impetus to development of new manufacturing pattern such as Agile Manufacture. So the networking of enterprise modeling system is also asked. Firstly we discuss the current research on this field. Then a new Networking Enterprise Modeling Infrastructure is brought forward in this paper. In this infrastructure, which has no limit on certain enterprise model architecture and adopts a peer-to-peer mode, each distributed enterprise is seen as a peer, but not a client or a server. It can join into a group freely and communicate with each group member and collaborate with them on Virtual Enterprise Modeling. A realizing clew based on COM is also given accompanying with the analysis of components.

articleTitle: A method of searching audio file query by example
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: We propose a method of searching audio files using query-by-example. Upon production of the best base, we expatriated the method which transforms the best base sub-space into the numerical value denote format of the best base sub-space. Using the numerical value denote format, we propose the crunode structure of the AVL-like search tree. Depending on the node structure, we propose the search method of the audio data in the best base, using the best base search to the AVL-like tree, to implement the credibility search in audio data. It is compared for the two methods of the proposed search arithmetic and the search method based on the wavelet transform by the tense, and the validity of the method is tested.

articleTitle: 3D feature recognition base on CNN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A 3D model feature recognition is an important problem in CIMS, and act as the bridge between CAD and CAM. With the topologic and complicated data of the 3D model, it is very difficult to find the feature. A constructive neural network is applied to the problem in the paper. The algorithm can recognize eight different simple features from each other, and can deal with some cross-feature. The result obtained indicates that the constructive neural network has significant ability in solving the problem of the feature recognition.

articleTitle: A performance recovery to robust H/sub /spl infin// control for generalized systems based on minimal function observer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the H/sub /spl infin// control problem for the generalized systems. If some conditions are satisfied, the generalized system can be generally stabilized by the state feedback. When the state variables can't all be measured, the minimal generalized function observer and the normal function observer are derived, and also the closed-loop system is still generally stable.

articleTitle: The operation optimization of AN reactor based on pattern recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Generally, research objects of chemical industry operation optimization are multi-factorial, highly noisy, nonlinear, non-Gaussian distributed, non-evenly distributed datasets which contain useful information for improving industrial processes. Optimization based on pattern recognition is a good tool of information mining. The paper gives the operation parameters of the acrylonitrile (AN) apparatus by applying an optimal method based on pattern recognition. The method can be applied to other industrial processes as well.

articleTitle: Study on an adaptive tabu search genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In order to solve the contradiction between reducing search space and keeping the diversity of evolution population in a genetic algorithm, an adaptive tabu search genetic algorithm is proposed. This algorithm adaptively changes the receiving probability of the tabu schema according to the diversity of evolution population, which not only reduces the search space and accelerates convergence speed but also efficiently avoids premature convergence. The simulation results show that the algorithm presented in the paper is effective.

articleTitle: Construction and application of a classifier system based on genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A kind of classifier systems based on genetic algorithms (GAs) is proposed. In the process of constructing the classifier system, the method uses GAs to adjust weights of all object attributes in all categories and membership functions of all categories synthetically to make them become harmonious and consistent. Finally, an experiment is conducted to demonstrate that this system is effective and practical.

articleTitle: A parameterization of all observers for linear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: By using a Luenberger reduced-order state observer and an auxiliary stable matrix, a modified parameterization of all linear observers is addressed. The factors of the observer parameterization are ensured to be stable and proper due to the use of the auxiliary stable matrix. Based on the proposed observer parameterization, the parameterization of estimation error dynamics is also developed.

articleTitle: A kind of fractal application for control message
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In the paper the fractal factor is proposed for a quantitative factor and for a proportional factor so that the fractal law can be used in fuzzy control by means of a look-up table. An example of the application shows that the control accuracy is improved.

articleTitle: Robust fault-tolerant control for linear systems with nonlinear uncertain parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The problem of robust fault-tolerant control for a class of linear systems with second-order uncertain parameters and a strong practical background is dealt with. A design method of a robust fault-tolerant feedback controller is given in terms of LMI. It has both integrity against actuator failure and robustness of parameter uncertainties.

articleTitle: Applications of neural network in the oxygen content prediction of boilers' smoke
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: On the background of the inefficient burning systems of boilers, neural network modeling techniques were studied intensively and presented to predict the oxygen content of boilers' smoke online. This pointed out a new way for improving the control of the burning systems. The problems arising from implementing a neural network model in real industrial processes are also considered and solved, including data collection, data pretreatment, soft model correction, and so on.

articleTitle: Study on soccer robot locomotor control rule
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: According to the character of soccer robot, sine proportional control rule is given in the paper. According to the fields where soccer robot moves, different sine control rules are given. Application shows that the method can overcome saturation and make soccer robot move more agilely and stably.

articleTitle: A CARMA model-based discrete-time variable structure controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, a discrete-time variable structure control is proposed. The control system is designed based on the CARMA model, so that steady-state precision is provided with robustness. This paper analyzes the effect of disturbance on the sliding-mode theoretically, and proposes an applied VSC law. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: The design and realization of the intelligent distant copy meter system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The intelligent distant copy meter system is an important solution to improve the automatic level of energy management. The system is based on the application of computer, and contains the technology of network, digital communication, sensors and micro-electronics and so on. It can be used for collecting and managing the amount of water, power, gas and the fees. The communication is realized by the local area network and the spread spectrum carrier wave of power line in the system.

articleTitle: Wavelet transform based optimal control of parameter-varying distributed parameter systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, an orthogonal function approximation approach has been employed to investigate the optimal distributed control of linear time-space varying distributed parameter systems. The product integrated operational matrix of Haar wavelets has been derived, so that the optimal distributed control problem for DPS can be converted to a lumped parameter problem by the wavelet transformation, and an approximation control algorithm for DPS has been obtained. Simulation results show the efficiency of the presented algorithm.

articleTitle: The design of extended product tree for quality check based on RDBMS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper presents a method to design the extended product tree for quality checking based on RDBMS, a new data structure in order to integrate checking information. It has been successfully used to design the extended product based on Oracle RDBMS which can store, check and query the data. The integration of quality information was successfully achieved.

articleTitle: A practical rough classifier for Chinese handwriting recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: It is very practical to apply multilevel classifier on solving large scale and complex recognition problems such as Chinese handwriting recognition. A multilevel classifier includes a high-level classifier (rough classifier) whose responsibility is to split patterns into different groups. In this paper, we design a novel rough classifier system that is used for Chinese handwriting recognition. Our algorithm is composed of two parts: clustering and classify. Our experiments show that the system achieves high precision on both training data and testing data.

articleTitle: A review of the measurement technique on the wetness fraction of turbine exhaust steam
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The wetness fraction is an important parameter that is closely related to the economy and safety of turbines. For application purposes, the development and current situation of wetness fraction measurement techniques are reviewed in this paper. Some typical methods are analyzed. The prospects for on-line measurement techniques of turbine exhaust steam are good.

articleTitle: Fuzzy extension information and intelligent transportation management-control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A highly efficient intelligent transportation system (ITS) is urgently needed to solve the transportation problems in large cites. Thus, new disciplines and approaches are necessary to be brought into the management and control of ITS. This paper introduces the application of fuzzy extension information in the management and control of intelligent transportation. It evaluates ITS with the fuzzy grey matter and element space decision support system. The method of fuzzy extension traffic control is proposed with the purpose of meeting the transportation requirement in large cities.

articleTitle: A multi-agent coordination communication paradigm in adversarial periodic team synchronization environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A communication paradigm is proposed for multi-agent coordination in dynamic, real time and adversarial PTS environment. This paper analyses the issues agent must solve for the purpose of better coordination and presents the design of paradigm. Finally, the application of the paradigm in RoboCup and MiroSot Simulated Soccer Game and the experiments demonstrate that our communication paradigm improved coordination in robots and increased the probability of winning game.

articleTitle: The control of closed soilless growing system in greenhouse agriculture
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A control strategy for control in a closed soilless growing system is investigated, considering the combination of sensor technology and expert system technology. In the paper, the method based on curve fitting is introduced to calculate the density of NO/sub 3//sup -/, K/sup +/, Ca/sup 2+/ and the value of pH and EC. Considering the complexity of plant nutrition, we present a model for the control of nutrition ingredient. The experiment results show that the strategy is effective.

articleTitle: A novel robust adaptive fuzzy controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: For a class of continuous-time nonlinear system, a novel robust adaptive fuzzy controller is proposed by using the Lyapunov method. It is proved that the control algorithm is globally stable, the output tracking-error of the system can convergence to a domain of zero under the assumptions. As a result, the system controlled has stronger robustness against the disturbance and modeling error.

articleTitle: The intelligent compound controller used in thermal power unit coordinated control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A new intelligent control method is presented for a unit coordinated control system in this paper. By an analysis of the dynamic characteristic of the unit, the intelligent compound controller is proposed for the problems in the system, such as the responding rate being slower for the goal load and the overshoot higher. The new controller that is employed in the coordinated control system of the thermal power unit is combined with fuzzy rules, the traditional feedback and feedforward controller and its parameters are tuned by the fuzzy rules. The simulation results and actual operation performance show that the control performance is improved. The ability of tracking and anti-jamming is enhanced, and the dynamic overshoot is decreased. It is in favor of the safety and stability of the unit.

articleTitle: MEA-based fuzzy self-adaptive control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: To improve the adaptability of a fuzzy controller, the performance of an I-F controller was analyzed, and by unifying its adjustable factor /spl alpha/ and integral coefficient /spl beta/, a MEA-fuzzy self-adaptive control structure is proposed in this paper. Parameters of /spl alpha/ and /spl beta/ can be optimized by MEA (Mind-Evolutionary Algorithm) to adapt to the changes of the environment. The simulation results have shown that the MEA-fuzzy adaptive control has a sound structure and improved control quality, which help in finding optimal parameters, improving system speed and reducing the steady error.

articleTitle: Construction and implementation of SEBI multiagent system model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, a society is divided into an estate, benefit group and individual based on different social benefits. In the light of this division, the society-estate-benefits group-individual multiagent system (SEBI MAS) model is introduced. To build the SEBI MAS, the agents in the system are decomposed into several function modules, such as the favorite address table, receiving coefficient unit, etc. With these modules, the agents can exchange information with each other, and the SEBI system can run in the mixed mode of autonomous and hierarchical administration. As a result, stability and flexibility of the system are obtained. The drawback that the mobile agent searching in the Internet or local area network cannot share the information with other agents is avoided. Finally, a typical example is given to illustrate the application of SEBI system. There are many interesting and challenging theoretical and practical issues in the SEBI MAS open to further research.

articleTitle: Robust H/sub /spl infin// control for time-delay systems with additive controller uncertainty
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper develops an H/sub /spl infin// control technique for uncertain linear time-delay systems, which takes account of not only plant uncertainty but also controller uncertainty. Considering additive controller gain variations, the paper focuses on the design of memoryless state feedback control such that the closed-loop system is quadratically stable and possesses an H/sub /spl infin// disturbance attenuation bound for all admissible uncertainties and arbitrary unknown delay. With the assumption that all the plant and controller uncertainties are described by time-varying but non-bounded form, the design method is presented based on algebraic Riccati inequality, and furthermore the obtained results can be transferred to the LAB problem based on Schur complements.

articleTitle: Nonlinear PID controller design based on GA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: When designing a nonlinear PID controller (NLPID), it is very difficulty to adjust its parameters because there are more than 9 parameters needed to be determined. This paper proposed a new method of designing a NLPID controller based on the genetic algorithm (GA).

articleTitle: The study of M/sub A/ active optics control system used for LAMOST
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) as one big-science project in the Ninth Five-Year Plan period (1996-2000) is a meridian reflecting Schmidt telescope. The MA active optics system is the key technique and the difficult point of LAMOST. In this paper, a distributed control system based on CANBUS is presented to be used for controlling the MA,and the framework and working of this distributed control system is discussed.

articleTitle: Constant quality rate control for content-based 3D wavelet video communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper presents a rate control algorithm designed for a content-based 3D wavelet video compression scheme. Wavelet compression schemes demand a rate control algorithm for real-time video communication systems. The new rate control algorithm manages the uncertain factors in both the size of the GOF and the network delay, and the new rate control algorithm is based on the leaky bucket approach, which employs a frame buffer for both the client and server sides. An intelligent buffering mechanism is developed on the client side to ensure the continuous display of reconstructed image frames. For the server side, a feedback mechanism is used from the client to control the server's buffer content and ensure that the acquisition rate of the server and display rate of the client are equal.

articleTitle: Research for application of group decision method on appraisement system of science research schema
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Appraisement of science research schema is a kind of group decision problem including multiple objects and multiple factors. In order to increase the level of science and impartiality of the appraisement, the paper studies the construction of a cascade index system and elimination method under asymmetry status, employs a fuzzy multiple hierarchy integrative judgement method to perform sorting and appraising of schemas, and argues for the method of combining Delphi and AHP to confirm the weight of the index.

articleTitle: Wavelet denoising in non gaussian noise using MDL principle
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Wavelet methods have succeeded in image denoising in gaussian noise. In non-gaussian noise, however, these methods will degrade drastically. By employing the MDL principle and a wavelet coefficient model, this paper discusses a study on image denoising in gaussian mixture noise. A new denoising scheme is derived and is based on per pixel detection. Experiment results show that the new scheme can not only denoise the image with small square error, but also provide a facility for the further compression.

articleTitle: The auto-tuning controller with low redundancy information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper introduces a new kind of auto-tuning controller. In order to get characteristic data for identifying the plant model, this kind of controller uses a method which is called "geometric progression growth recording method". By the method, the redundancy information of the sample data can be minimized, while the size of data memory can be reduced, and the controller can adapt itself to the different response speed of different plants.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of adaptive modulation in slow fading Rayleigh channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Adaptive modulation can improve both the energy and spectral efficiency. In this paper, the performance analysis of BER and BPS based on adaptive modulation between BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM and 64QAM are given. Simulation shows that the result of adaptive modulation are better than that of fixed modulation.

articleTitle: Advanced control and optimization techniques applied to industrial processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: After analyzing the importance of advanced control and optimization techniques applied to industrial processes, this paper presents those successful application examples completed by the authors in recent years. The practical problems encountered in real application are also discussed.

articleTitle: Computer intelligent resource management system for CIMS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The important role of manufacture resource management system for CIMS is outlined first. Then, according to the need of CIMS, which was implemented in a large enterprise, the design idea, structure and functions of intelligent manufacture resource management system for CIMS are represented and some key technologies of the system are introduced.

articleTitle: A designing method of hierarchical fuzzy systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A hierarchical fuzzy system is an effective method to solve "rule explosion" when using a fuzzy controller. However, there are still a lot of problems to be solved when we design and structurally identify the system. Based on other scholars' researches the authors bring forward a new method of combining the genetic algorithm with least square estimation. The simulation shows the new algorithm is effective.

articleTitle: Hybrid intelligent control algorithm to ship steering based on soft computing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A hybrid intelligent technique is used for ship steering control in this paper. GA optimization is used for the off-line learning period. According to the new definition of fitness function, the optimized result obtained is more suitable to the actual situation. In an online learning period, the reinforcement learning and neural fuzzy control are integrated. It removes the drawback of the conventional hybrid intelligent algorithm that learning must be provided with some sample data, and the ship control quality is effectively improved in the case of appending additional sea state disturbance.

articleTitle: Wavelet packet-based modulating identification and its application in TE process
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Wavelet-based modulation identification is commonly used to build models. Since orthogonal wavelet transform operates only on the coarse part of the data series while keeping the detail part unchanged, it limits analyzing delicately. For this cause, we put forward the matrix expression of orthogonal wavelet packet transform, and discuss the modulating identification principle based on wavelet packet. It shows that this improved method is the equivalence of least squares method without weighting, and formulation with weighting is put forward based on the established rules. At last this method is applied to TE (Tennessee Eastman) process successfully.

articleTitle: Credit-risk decision mechanism (CRDM) with incentive effect under asymmetry information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, we consider that there are two types of loan entrepreneurs in a society: one is high-risk type and the other is low-risk type. We study the credit-risk decision mechanism (CRDM) with an incentive effect under asymmetric information. We introduce the theory and method of incentive mechanism for the research. We establish a credit-risk decision model from the point of view of the risk minimization of credit money. We give both the incentive compatibility constraints and individual rationality constraints. In addition, we also derive a sufficient and necessary conclusion that the bank offers the same rationing to the two types.

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation of passive target tracking algorithm under polar coordinates
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Due to the inborn non-linearity and observability problem, passive tracking is more difficult than active tracking, and the conventional algorithms cannot be applied to passive tracking directly. First, a brief review of the research work conducted on observability is given, then a traditional passive tracking algorithm under polar coordinates and its deficiencies are analyzed. A target maneuver detector is added to the traditional passive tracking algorithm and Monte-Carlo simulation shows that the proposed algorithm could successfully track objects moving with piece-wise constant velocity. Finally, future research areas are pointed out.

articleTitle: Security sheath and intelligence countermeasure in emergency of intricacy system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This text explores the process of responding to an emergency, and how to apply each artificial intelligence technique thereto. 1. Set up a security boundary sheath model of the system, use the "KDD" (knowledge discovery system) to search the badness of unexpected events which is about to break out, prevent it actively; 2. Make a whole analysis of the system in which happened the emergency, to prevent further problems; 3. Make use of the "extension analysis" and "genetic algorithms" to search and optimize whole condition. At last, present the rim picture of solve unexpected events discussed with artificial intelligence technique.

articleTitle: The existence of equilibrium solution of the nonlinear dynamic input-output stochastic model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper proposes a nonlinear dynamic input-output stochastic model. By using the degree theory on finite-dimensional space, in nonlinear analysis the condition for the existence of equilibrium solution is obtained and an estimate formula about the maximum equilibrium rate of national economic growth is provide.

articleTitle: Robust stabilization for perturbed discrete time-delay large-scale systems via dynamic output feedback control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Robust stabilization problem for a class of perturbed discrete large-scale systems with time-delays is discussed in this paper. Decentralized dynamic output feedback controllers and the tolerable bounds can be obtained simultaneously by means of a convex optimization involving linear matrix inequality. In addition, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is shown by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Robust H/sub /spl infin// filter design for uncertain linear systems with state delay
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of robust H/sub /spl infin// filtering for linear systems with state delay and parameter uncertainty. State delay exists in both state equations and measurement equations. The sufficient condition of the existence for the robust filter is derived and parameterized by the modified Riccati inequalities. For all admissible uncertainties, the filtering process remains robustly stable and the transfer function meets the prescribed H/sub /spl infin//-norm upper-bound constraints. The simulation example shows the validity and the applicability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: The design of pre-estimating neural network model for high-impedance electric arc furnace
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Introduces the characteristics and method of the intelligent-type computer control system of a high-impedance electric arc furnace, and then focuses on the designing of a pre-estimating neural network model including the application of genetic algorithms in establishing a neural network model and the requirement of real time study for a neural network model. It is verified that this system has a series of advantages such as high efficiency, low consumption of energy, electrodes and refractories through practical operation.

articleTitle: Application of universal learning network to the pH neutralization process identification
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The pH neutralization process is a typical nonlinear system, and the control and identification of such process is one of the difficult problems. It is difficult to identify such process using the traditional identification method at present. In this paper a new type of neural network, called the universal learning network, is used to identify this process. The method is easy to realize with satisfactory precision.

articleTitle: An improved method for detecting and identifying gross errors simultaneously
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A linear combination technology is applied to identify gross errors (bias and leaks) and estimate their magnitude in a linear steady state process. A linear combination scheme is used firstly to isolate the candidate subset of gross errors and then simultaneous identification/estimation of gross errors is accomplished. Comparative studies of performance is performed on a recycle network and a steam system simulation results show that the proposed approach has higher performance for identifying gross errors as well as to estimate their magnitude.

articleTitle: Neural-net-based modeling used in the ASP complicated flooding systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Constructs models of the nonlinear functional relationships between the petrophysical properties of rocks and their electrical properties and of the ASP complicated flooding systems based on neural networks. The learning algorithm is a kind of variable metric method, and it has fast convergence rate and good precision. The research result shows that the method is suitable for the modeling and identification of nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: From modern philosophy to intelligent robot
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Thinking and intelligence can never be separated from the world. Modern philosophy rests on a new interpretation of the nature and fulfillment of human reason, and disputes about the nature of human reason are the ultimate battles of philosophy. The symbol based AI approach is not practical for real world problems. The world is artificial intelligence's best model. Intelligence can only be determined by the dynamics of interaction with the world. Being is a temporal event inseparable from the understanding of being embodied in Dasein's forms of life. Based on the modern philosophy's spirit, the behavior-based systems interact with real world directly. The constructed AI system based on philosophy has to express all its goals and desires as physical action to affect its environment, and extract all its knowledge from physical sensors. In this study, a fully autonomous mobile robot is built, after a thorough research to the philosophy's origin of the modern AI. In the mobile robot developed, each module itself generates behavior, and improvement in the competence of the system proceeds by adding new modules to the system. The performance of the robot proves that the whole system is stable.

articleTitle: Learning control of failure avoidance problems with known analytical form of cost function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: We study adaptive critic designs for a class of failure avoidance control problems. We categorize such problems by the choice of local cost function as zero throughout a trial except at the last time step when a failure occurs. We derive an analytical form of its overall cost function defined as the infinite summation of the local cost function over time. We demonstrate that the outputs of the critic network after learning resemble well the analytically derived cost function.

articleTitle: A sufficient optimality condition for bang-bang controls on local time-optimal control problems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: We study L/sub /spl infin//-local optimality of a given control u/spl tilde/(.) in the time-optimal control problem for an affine control system. By means of Lie series, we establish a sufficient optimality condition for bang-bang controls.

articleTitle: Method of parameters identification of imaging model used to correct computer vision error
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: An imaging channel's nonlinear characteristic is one of the factors of computer vision error. Common methods of distortion correction rely on a lot of prior knowledge and interactive information. As the imaging model is only related to the structure of the vision system, and the parameters of the model can be identified automatically, it has a prevalent significance to correct computer vision error using an imaging model. The paper gives an example of a micro robot soccer vision system, using an imaging model, identifying parameters and gaining good results.

articleTitle: The optimal control for the output feedback stochastic system under the risk-sensitive cost
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The optimal control problem for partially observable stochastic system is considered. The dynamics has the linear affine form and the explicit output feedback control law for this system under the risk-sensitive cost is derived by means of change of probability and 'complete of squares'. This enables one to convert the partially observable problems into equivalent complete observable control problems and use the usual ways to solve them.

articleTitle: The learning algorithm of constructive NN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: We give a learning algorithm of a constructive neural network (CNN) which is a novel neural network model. With the advantages coming from the CNN, the learning algorithm can estimate and get the accurate pattern spatial distribution. First, an introduction to the CNN is given. Then the learning algorithm of the CNN is designed. Finally, the result of an example is shown and some suggestions are given.

articleTitle: Research on application of field bus-based data acquisition and intelligent sensing technology in robot teleoperation system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The data acquisition and intelligent sensing network plays an important role in a robot teleoperation system. It is composed of sensing, controlling, computing, information processing, network communication, artificial intelligence and many other technologies. Compared with the traditional method, great changes have taken place in the design and production of intelligent sensors and actuators. Its future development direction is networking with intelligent interfaces. The article introduces the theory and application of field bus-based data acquisition and intelligent sensing technology in robot teleoperation system. It also discusses several key problems and corresponding solutions in this issue.

articleTitle: Weighting adaptive control of Wiener model based on multilayer feedforward neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The parameter identification and control method of a typical class of nonlinear systems-Wiener model is studied. A two-step method is proposed to estimate the linear and nonlinear parts. The proposed identification model is made up of a linear autoregressive moving average model in cascade with a multilayer feedforward neural network. The nonlinearity effects can be eliminated by using the classical extended minimum variance self-tuning control strategy of linear systems. The correction of the proposed control algorithm is verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: A new algorithm of fuzzy on-line identification for nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A new fuzzy on-line identification algorithm for a nonlinear dynamic system is presented. This method combines the conventional on-line identification with fuzzy logic system. The nonlinear system is approximated by a set of fuzzy rules that describe the local linear dynamic in each subspace formed by fuzzifying the input and output space. The fuzzy space of input variables is partitioned by means of diagonal ANFIS method, the consequent parameters of the fuzzy rules are identified by means of weighted recursive least squares algorithm (WRLSA). The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method is practical and efficient.

articleTitle: Research on recognition algorithm of moving-target on the battlefield
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A new target recognition algorithm based on the combination of radar and acoustic sensors is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the velocity, the first dominant frequency and the second dominant frequency of the target are taken as effective characteristics, and then the expression of the basic probability assignment function for the target character is obtained though fuzzy inference. Secondly, D-S evidential reasoning is applied to the combination of characteristics to get the reliable recognition of the target. Lastly, simulation is performed on the new algorithm, and the simulation results prove the algorithm is effective.

articleTitle: DFBR field image model based scene navigability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The deficiency of analyzing aircraft's scene navigability where scene is modeled by Gauss random field is set forth. Wavelet analysis has well time-frequency trait and multiresolution property, which provides an ideal tool for studying the fine content of an image. Based on the wavelet representation, discrete Fractal Brownian Random field is presented as scene's model. Discrete fractal Brownian random field embodies the relation of details at different resolutions. Experiments show that this representation is significant. Then the novel application of this model in analyzing scene navigability is given.

articleTitle: The design and realization on control system of micro-arrays printing instrument
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The paper introduces the design, hardware structure and software realization of gene chip micro-arrays printing instrument. We discuss the editing method of the control process. We achieve the graphics mode design of the gene chips layout and chip structure. The control system can optimize the route of micro-arrays printing in spite of the chips layout and chip structure. It speeds up the microarrays printing instrument performance.

articleTitle: On the properties of 3D grasping forces: theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, we introduced the concept of the force concentration line in analyzing the force distribution among the grasping fingers in 3D four-fingered grasps. The characteristics of the force concentration lines and the relationship between these lines and the principal axes are discussed. A new representation of the finger forces is proposed and the equilibrium grasping forces can be expressed and determined clearly using this representation. It turns out, that, using this new representation scheme, we can solve all the possible solutions to the grasping force distribution problem.

articleTitle: Expert system for the calculation of building's design cooling load based on artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In the stage of schematic design, some data needed to calculate design cooling load can not be supplied with accurate values, designers have to assess a value according to their experience only. The calculation of a building's design cooling load is different from the load analysis of existing buildings, it is a prediction of the maximum possible load of a future building when it is put into use, so it has the characteristic of uncertainty and prediction. In order to improve calculation efficiency and enhance accuracy, expert system technology is introduced and incorporated with a load index assessment method. Consequently, an expert system for the calculation of a building's design cooling load is established on the basis of artificial neural network theories. Application examples indicate that this system is simple and workable; the calculation results thereof achieve high accuracy, and calculation methods are in conformity to the thinking habits of designers.

articleTitle: Robust stability analysis of Takagi-Sugeno discrete-times fuzzy control systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, a robust stability analysis method for the well-known discrete Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy model is presented. Based on the fuzzy controller, which is designed by a fuzzy system with no uncertainty, some new robust stability conditions giving a stability-guaranteed parametric uncertainty range are given for the fuzzy controller and fuzzy system with uncertainty. Some estimations for the range of uncertainty is given for a SISO fuzzy system wherein the stability of the total system is guaranteed. The effectiveness of the proposed analysis method is illustrated by a simple example.

articleTitle: The design and implementation of an excellent text categorization system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Based on the study of text classification techniques, a new text categorization method which uses a weight adjustment measure to improve a vector space model and naive Bayesian classifier is proposed, and an experimental text classification system CWZ is implemented to make comparison within various text classification approaches. Compared with many commercial text classification systems, the behavior of CWZ is much better. We introduce its framework, function, main modules and running environment, give our experimental results, and discuss a few important technical issues involved in the system to get some valuable conclusions. We also describe how to improve the vector space model and naive Bayesian classifier.

articleTitle: Robust reliable H/sub /spl infin// control for time-varying uncertain systems with time-delay
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the robust reliable H/sub /spl infin// controller design problem for a class of nonlinear time-varying uncertain systems with time-delay and unknown nonlinear disturbances. The linear memoryless dynamic output feedback controller based on a state observer is designed such that, for all admissible uncertainties as well as actuator failures occurring among a prescribed subset of actuators, the closed-loop system is quadratically stable with an H/sub /spl infin// norm bound constraint. An illustrative example and simulation results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: A kind of flowshop schedule problem with uncertain processing time
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In the production scheduling of industrial processes, there are various uncertainties, and the uncertainty of processing time is the most typical one. In this paper, the uncertainty of processing time is described as triangle fuzzy numbers, and the scheduling model for flow-shop processing under uncertainty is established based on the fuzzy programming theory. The fuzzy programming is converted into distinct single-objective programming by employing the two fuzzy operations given by Masatoshi et al. (1999) and the "middle maximal membership" algorithm presented by the authors (2000). The experimental study validates the efficiency of the proposed scheduling model and fuzzy optimization method, and the influence of the decision factor /spl Gamma/ is discussed.

articleTitle: Smart collision free motion control for robot arms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A novel collision free motion control scheme is presented for robot arms operating in dynamic environment. The motion control action consists of two parts: goal reaching (GR) and collision avoidance (CA). During execution, the GR action is produced by a potential field-type method (or by human operators in teleoperation), and the CA action is taken by a local-global strategy presented here. Firstly the robot links with collision potential are evaluated and proper CA actions are produced separately for these links without considering other parts of the robot. Then, a global fusion mechanism synthesizes all of these local commands to meet the CA requirement from every link facing potential collisions. The fusion policy is giving higher priority to the link with higher collision probability. The local-global strategy takes full advantages of robot freedom to realize more smart CA actions and dexterous performance in complex environment. Another merit of this method is to drastically simplify the design of whole robot body CA.

articleTitle: An application on a Parkinson's disease diagnosis based on inductive reasoning algebra
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The paper first introduces the form and the rules system of the inductive reasoning algebra, and then the logic analysis of the Parkinson's disease diagnosis is provided by applying inductive reasoning algebra. We disclose the total logic connotation of the diagnosis, and indicate the feasibility of application.

articleTitle: Iterative learning control with an optimality criterion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: An improved iterative learning control based on optimality criterion is proposed in this paper. The control signal in each trial is calculated as the solution of a minimum norm optimization problem with a reasonable performance index. The convergence of the tracking error sequence and input sequence can be proved by the properties of optimality criterion instantly. The iterative learning control algorithm of linear time-varying system assures that the input sequence will converge to the optimal control of linear quadratic tracking problem. The algorithm achieves an exponential rate of convergence. The theory of the proposed algorithm is verified through the comparison in the simulation studies.

articleTitle: Evolutionary optimal control of free floating spacecraft
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: To control the free floating spacecraft in outer space, this paper builds a model of free floating sphere movement under the action or multi-thrusters, and uses genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the path and position in different control phases by using a combination of thrusters. In each phase, it makes the control target as the fitness function of GA to search the best solution, then uses this combination to move the sphere to an objective position and stabilizes it in the objective state. Contrasted to the traditional optimal control method, this control method is much simple and does not need a complicated algorithmic analysis, but can achieve a much effective result.

articleTitle: Mixed H/sub 2//H/sub /spl infin// control for linear singular systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper considers the mixed H/sub 2//H/sub /spl infin// control problem for linear singular systems. The sufficient condition to the existence of a mixed H/sub 2//H/sub /spl infin// output feedback controller is given in terms of LMIs. The controller guarantees that the closed-loop system is impulse-free and stable, satisfies the H/sub /spl infin// performance, and minimizes the H/sub 2/ performance subject to these three constraints.

articleTitle: Adaptive actuator failure compensation for feedback linearizable systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)

articleTitle: A design of a low cost high precision data acquisition system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The paper presents a high precision data acquisition system with the LM231 V/F transform chip and a low cost single chip microcomputer. The V/F transformer features high precision, high linearity and with a simple peripheral circuit. The single chip microcomputer is connected directly to an interface with the LM231 chip that has a lower-power coupling circuit, to improve the system working reliability. Fully utilised the hardware and software resources, the system identifier rate reaches 12 digits and its accurate is 0.02%. The system is available for use in the field of measurements of a weighing system, voltage, current intensity, methane density, etc. In the case of long connecting distance between the sensors and upper computer, the RS-485 interface or wireless data transmitting/receiving module can be used to realise remote data communication.

articleTitle: The identification of frequency domain model of ultrasonic vibration system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The identification of frequency domain model of ultrasonic vibration system by using least square method is discussed. The key frequency band is subdivided, in order to keep characteristic point of system invariability. An actual vibrating body is checked up, and the model coincides with the experiment result well. This identifying model can be extensively applied to many fields.

articleTitle: The ideas of feature-based parametric modeling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper introduces the application of parametric design to feature and feature-based modeling to form parametric feature and realize modeling parametrically. With OOP, the required information is capsulated and new feature can be derived from old one by inheritance. This method integrates the abundance of feature information and the encapsulation and inheritance of OOP.

articleTitle: The model and algorithm of automatic data-mining of network intrusion characteristics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The paper is focused on the study of the automatic data mining of network intrusion features, its modeling and consequently provides the optimized solving algorithm. The effectiveness of the model and algorithm is tested through the feature data mining of the attack which exploits the IIS (Internet Information Server) vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Smith online identification predictive control and its application in STM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, a Smith online identification predictive control method was proposed for the system with delay. As we know, the Smith predictor, put forward by Smith (1959), resolves how to control the object with delay theoretically. However, due to the existing modeling error, a good control effect cannot be be acquired. It is even impossible to design a proper controller in order to stabilize the system. This paper incorporates system identification with the Smith predictor to-realize Smith online identification prediction control to compensate the delay. The identification module models the object dynamically. Based on the result, the delay is compensated by the Smith predictor. Experiments are presented to demonstrate that the method is of strong self-adaptability. Furthermore, it was successfully applied in the compensation control system of the AJ-I scanning tunneling microscope (STM) manufactured by Shanghai Aijian Nanometer science & technology development Ltd.

articleTitle: Theoretical and simulation research on real-time path tracking strategy for industrial robots
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Previously, researchers raised the accuracy of robot hand tracking a specified path in Cartesian space mainly through increasing the number of the path's segments. However, this method resulted in the heavier online computational burden for the robot controller. In this paper, aiming at this drawback, the authors propose a new kind of real-time and accurate hand path tracking method for robots. Through selecting some extra knots on the specified hand path by a certain rule, which enables the number of knots on each segment to increase from two to four, and through introducing a sinusoidal function and cosinoidal function to the joint displacement equation of each segment, this method can greatly raise the path tracking accuracy of a robot hand, and does not change the number of the path's segments and the sum of joint displacement equations. It also does not increase markedly the computational burden of the robot controller. The result of computer simulation shows this method is very effective.

articleTitle: A modified continuous genetic algorithm and its application for job-shop scheduling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The continuous genetic algorithm has a risk for long staying on one stage before it gains the best solution. This paper presents the modified continuous genetic algorithm to overcome this disadvantage. This algorithm is applied to job-shop scheduling to test its validity. The test results show this algorithm is good at operation and convergence.

articleTitle: A hierarchical global path planning approach for AUV
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Proposes a hierarchical global path planning approach for an autonomous underwater vehicle in an ocean. This approach consists of successive decomposition of the robot's workspace and searching for a path at each level of decomposition. In the process of heuristic search, the evaluation function takes into account both the energy cost and the length of paths. The approach proves to be flexible and practicable, and can reduce memory consumption significantly.

articleTitle: The application of real-time expert control system to large scale PTA plant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The P-xylene oxidation unit is the key part of PTA (pure terephthalic acid) plant. Due to many uncertain factors such as non-linearity, strong coupling etc., it is hard for traditional control strategies to fulfill the operation objectives. To solve these problems, a kind of real-time expert control system (RECS) is proposed. The successful application of the proposed PECS to a PTA plant in a chemical factory shows that the RECS can not only overcome the real-time problems that perplexed the conventional expert system, by close combination with the HONEYWELL TDC-3000 DCS internal system and friendly man-machine interface, it is also more convenient for operation and correction of an expert knowledge database.

articleTitle: Fuzzy reasoning mathematics model and stability analysis of nonlinear control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In recent years, good results have been achieved by using the designation idea of fuzzy control systems to deal with nonlinear control objects, but the designation of the fuzzy control system faces the problems of fuzzy control rules and the system stability analysis. This paper proposes to use the fuzzy mathematical model based on fuzzy reasoning to analyze the stability, applying genetic algorithms (GA) to adjust the fuzzy control rules, simulating the method of classical control theory which uses a mathematical model of the control objects to analyze the stability. Its efficiency is shown by the example in the paper.

articleTitle: Controller performance assessment and monitoring - theory and its applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Controller performance assessment is a challenging task in industrial process control. In this work, we review the state of research in controller performance assessment and monitoring, and present some commercial implementations of the technology in process industries. Challenges related to the controller performance evaluation are outlined for research and applications.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous multi-processors scheduling by coevolutionary genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: The efficacy and efficiency of conventional single population-based evolutionary algorithms (CEAs) decrease with the number of independent tasks in heterogeneous multi-processors systems. Based on computational model of cooperative coevolution, a task matching and scheduling algorithm is proposed for heterogeneous multi-processors systems, and the computation of individual's fitness is given according to the cooperative interactions among species. Simulation results show that the coevolutionary genetic algorithm is more effective than CEA for multi-tasks matching and scheduling, and the algorithm is of practical use in engineering.

articleTitle: The application of floating encode genetic algorithms in finding optimal multivariable
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Gives a method for studying a fuzzy controller based on floating encoded genetic algorithms. Research on the efficiency of binary encoding and floating encoding is demonstrated. By an example the high efficiency of floating encoded genetic algorithms is shown.

articleTitle: A study on intelligent fault diagnosis in engine room by Bayes method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Traditional monitoring equipment can only give warning when a fault was detected. This paper focuses on an intelligent fault diagnosis system in an engine room. By using the anteriority Bayes data fusion and statistical inference method, we can build a fault knowledge base and inference rules, and predict and fast diagnose causes of the fault. This method of intelligent diagnosis is suitable to those equipments that have their own fault regulations. The article also applies these theories into practices in an engine room.

articleTitle: Guaranteed cost robust predictive control for discrete uncertain time-delay systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of robust control is investigated for a class of discrete uncertain time-delay systems subject to input and state constraints. A guaranteed cost robust predictive control scheme is presented, which combines a quasi-infinite horizon predictive control scheme and guaranteed cost robust control as well as the finite terminal weighting matrix method to deal with the problems of input and state constraints and system uncertainty. The sufficient conditions of stability are presented. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The auto guarding system against theft for pipeline transportation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This article discusses the principle and structure of the auto guarding system against theft used in oil or gas pipelines transportation. The system can collect, process and identify abnormal sound through sound processing technology, the frequency width of the system can be ascertained by analyzing the power spectrum of the simulated abnormal sound. The structure of wireless communication network used in this system is also introduced. The system is stable, the correct recognition ratio can reach 100%, and the error warning ratio is below 1%.

articleTitle: Disturbance rejection performance of generalized predictive control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Discussion about disturbance rejection properties of generalized predictive control (GPC) is provided in the form of pole-placement and internal model control structure. It is pointed out that the nonzero mean noise signal of the open loop has become a stationary noise signal in a closed loop, and that GPC is robust with respect to steady-state offset in the measured variable from the set point. Based on the closed loop transfer functions of disturbance channels and the frequency properties of GPC, it is demonstrated that the use of an observer polynomial T can give enhanced robustness against high frequency noise and unmodelled dynamics and enabled independent tailoring of set-point and disturbance responses.

articleTitle: Disturbance decoupling problem of state feedback model predictive control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: For state feedback model predictive control system design, the disturbance decoupling problem is studied in detail. For the undetectable or immeasurable disturbance, necessary and sufficient conditions are given for the disturbance decoupling problem design of the state feedback model predictive control system. We consider the disturbance decoupling problem and state space model, the design procedures are given step by step for choosing the design parameter-the prediction horizon. A simulation example is given, the simulation result shows that both the control performance and the disturbance rejection ability are improved and the control system design procedures are effective.

articleTitle: Research on conflict resolution based on multi-agent system in concurrent engineering
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A kind of intelligent conflict-resolving system based on multi-agents is put forward after analyzing the existing methods of conflict resolution. The function and architecture of each agent are discussed. The concept, cause and classification are briefly explained. Finally, the system was implemented in an electronic company and showed good effectiveness.

articleTitle: Adaptive integration control with satisfactory transients for uncertain linear system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: It is well known that if the steady-state gain G(0) of a stable lumped system, with transfer function G(s), is positive, then compensating the system by an integral controller k/s, where k is a gain parameter, leads to a stable closed-loop system which achieves tracking of arbitrary constant reference signals, provided that the gain parameter k is positive and sufficiently small. An existing adaptive version of the above result for the class of stable lumped systems, can achieve asymptotically tracking, but can not robustly achieve satisfactory transients for any system of this class. In this paper we derive an adaptive version with self-learning iteration of the above result for the class of stable lumped systems, so that asymptotically tracking and satisfactory transients are achieved for any system of this class.

articleTitle: Wavelet packets analysis of rolling bearing vibration signal and fault testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Proposes a method for fault testing on a rolling bearing based on wavelet transformation and pattern recognition. Wavelet packets decomposition is used to extract features of dynamic vibration information; K-NN is introduced to test the fault on a rolling bearing. Experiments show that the proposed method attains a satisfactory effect.

articleTitle: Maximum algebra of random variables with its applications in discrete event systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A maximum algebra of random variables, which can be used to analyse the manufacturing processes in discrete event stochastic dynamic systems, is presented. A kind of series-parallel production line systems in which the work durations of all tasks are random variables with exponential distributions is discussed. By means of the maximum algebra of random variables the statistical characteristics of total manufacturing time are obtained in order to estimate its production performance. An example is given for confirming the validity of the method by comparing it with the result of simulation.

articleTitle: Adaptive backstepping control for a class of strict feedback nonlinear systems using radial basis neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: Addresses the problem of designing robust output tracking control for strict-feedback nonlinear systems with unknown nonlinear functions and unknown virtual coefficient nonlinear functions using radial basis neural networks. By defining desired control, a smooth and singularity-free adaptive controller is firstly designed for a first-order plant. Then, an extension is made to high-order nonlinear systems using neural network approximation, adaptive backstepping techniques and robust control. No upper bounds of unknown virtual coefficient functions are required. The effects of approximation error and unknown upper bounds of virtual coefficient functions are counteracted by adaptive robust terms. It is shown that under the proposed adaptive control the tracking error of the controlled system converges to a small neighborhood around zero. Simulation examples are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: The research on the displaying methods of visual digital terrain based on DEM data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A digital elevation model (DEM) is convenient for representing the continuously varying topographic surface of the Earth, and it is a common data source for terrain analysis and other spatial applications. In the mean time, the utility of visual digital terrain is widespread. Thus, methods used for displaying visual digital terrain based on DEM data were to be researched carefully. The paper presents a method of reading the USGS standard format DEM data and gives two ways of displaying the digital terrain's surface. Triangle mesh is a common and widely used method and has its own merits in displaying, while constructing surface using NURBS curve is another important way. Their difference and similarities was noted. Examples of these two displaying methods were also presented.

articleTitle: A new type of reconfigurable control against actuator faults
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: A new type of reconfigurable control strategy based on fault detection and diagnosis by using a model following method is presented. The method can make the outputs of a failing system exactly track those of a reference model by detecting the location and amplitude of failure of an actuator failure, modify control parameters, and redesign the control law online to counteract dynamics caused by actuator failure. The method is easy to carry out, and following accuracy is higher.

articleTitle: On fuzzy inference and control for nonlinear system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: This paper is concerned with building models from fuzzy information and with reasoning with such information. The paper investigates the synthesis structure of fuzzy control in the nonlinear system, known as the universal approximation property. Some discussions on the sensitivity of the design of fuzzy systems are provided. The main theoretical result is the approximation capability of fuzzy systems.

articleTitle: Reduction of the RoboCup state space
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
abstract: As a standard research platform of artificial intelligence and robotics, RoboCup is gathering more and more attention. Because in the match, the environment is dynamically changing, the method of machine learning is widely used. An important problem is how to reduce the complex environment in learning, so that the number of states is decreased. The paper briefly introduces Soccer Server. Then several methods of constructing the state space are analyzed. A method of reduction of the state space is described. The method divides the environment around the client into some regions which are not equal in size. The state space is constructed with these regions.

articleTitle: Augmented Lagrange multiplier based fuzzy evolutionary algorithm and application for constrained optimization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 4th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.02EX527)
